_comment: Explicit exceptions to the local clock-gating rules (tools/check-cg.py, docs/rtl-coding-style.md 'Local clock gating'), written by the module's owner. One entry per module, rule (CG-1, CG-2, CG-3, CG-4, CG-5 or RST-1) and register: module, rule, target, why, by, date. why says what was measured and why the rule cannot or should not be met. A CG-5 waiver also carries ports, the input ports it lets into the enable, and enable_ngd, the enable's total depth: the latest port's arrival plus the cone, within CCV_NGD_CG_EN (OI-59). A waiver carries its threshold and fails again past it (Daniel; OA's response OI-66): a CG-3 waiver states floor_pct and measured_pct, each by scenario (idle, medium, high), the floor 2 points under the measurement and never over it, and optionally enable, the one gate of its register it takes, by its enable's name as check-cg reports it (OI-66); an allowance waiver, for CG-1's registers written every cycle or CG-4's ungated flops, states max_flops and measured_flops. A waiver of flops that hold an interface lead signal, any rule, carries lead: true, and one of flops that capture a credit-return pulse carries credit: true; their flops count against the block's 2% per instance (Daniel's rulings on RI-15 and RI-14, 2026-11-06, RA revs 87 and 88; RI-17). A waiver that excuses nothing is refused; one beside a ratchet entry supersedes it.

waivers.why: OA's response OI-58: a timer's grant has no lead (the grant register's D is select's pick at 24.3 NGD, and the issue loop cannot pay a cycle). The grant comes from ooe_sched's third (* keep *) copy of its grant register (grant_w_cq04h), for this module alone, at 1 NGD (ooe_wake.ngd.json; OA's response re:OI-122, rev 375). Under C9h the hint match is decoded from the raw capture inside the enable: check-cg measures each timer's enable cone at 6.1 NGD at worst, 7.1 in all with the grant's arrival, within CG-2's 8. Every other term of the enable is this module's own flops (OA's responses OI-58, OI-62).

OA's response OI-65 (OA tab, 2026-10-21, rev 156): the group of each slot's take, count and valid bits (14 flops) is clocked by rename's per-slot take-enable, deq_sel_cq01h (a superset of its take, from rename's flops at 2.0 NGD, ooe_decq.ngd.json; the superset is asserted, deq_sel_covers), or the slot's own transit, arrival and flush flops. check-cg measures the cone at 2.0 to 2.2 NGD, 4.2 in all with the arrival, within CG-2's 8. One enable shared by the slots gave 61 to 71% DCGE; per slot, 90% and over. It replaces OI-58's "some warp takes" waiver of about 5 (deq_any_cq01h, dropped).

OA's response OI-65 (OA tab, 2026-10-21, rev 156): the group of each slot's payloads and admission bits (82 flops) is clocked by rename's per-slot take-enable, deq_sel_cq01h (a superset of its take, from rename's flops at 2.0 NGD, ooe_decq.ngd.json; the superset is asserted, deq_sel_covers), or the slot's own transit, arrival and flush flops. check-cg measures the cone at 2.0 to 2.2 NGD, 4.2 in all with the arrival, within CG-2's 8. One enable shared by the slots gave 61 to 71% DCGE; per slot, 90% and over. It replaces OI-58's "some warp takes" waiver of about 5 (deq_any_cq01h, dropped).

DA's decision (a), OA's response OI-66 (OA tab rev 179): the allowances held (20 flops, one-hot per credit) are recomputed every cycle from rename's pool and floors and the warps with a head; enabled on any slot's change bit, they change on 66% (medium) and 54% (high) of enabled cycles, measured at 8ef3dff; idle enables none. Floors 2 under. Re-measured by TI with RA-43's L1_CMPL 18 (the bench's model traffic moves; ooe_go's RTL has no latency in it): 65% and 51.9%, so the floors follow, 2 under (OI-18: OI to confirm).

OA's rev 219 (OI-76): the names' pool registers (GPR and predicate, 10 flops) are formed from the remainders as they stand, less the older take, so they must be clocked while a names' take is registered and on the edge after the remainders move (nv), not with the counters alone; the bench holds every take to the model's and the scarce build's no-take-q2 control fails without the older take. They change on few of those cycles: the GPR pool stands at its saturation XM while names are plentiful, and the predicates' at the pool less its floors while no slot holds past its floor. Measured 12% (medium) and 24% (high); idle enables none. Clocked with the counters instead, under their enable or nv, the 175-flop gate fell to 68% in medium (96% high); skipping nv while both pools stand at XM leaves it there, the predicates' pool never reaching XM. Each pool alone would be a 5-flop gate, past the module's allowance (19 of its 23.9 flops in use). Floors 2 under the measure.

The candidates' rows and valids (72 flops), one gate: the valids clocked on the rows' enable, the reset among its terms (DA's grant, OA's direction, DA tab rev 94). OI-81 (a) and OI-82 (OA's revs 252-254; granted by DA, 2026-10-25): each slot's two home-position candidates, the lowest owned live row with its home section or home pair free, found over all 192 rows and registered. The find's result is stable while the section bits move under it, so the candidates change on few of the cycles a section changes; the only exact enable is the 192-row find itself, and no enable from the module's own flops within CCV_NGD_CG_EN reaches 75% (a per-slot enable, measured on the model, sees a candidate change on 17-20% of its events). Without them Rename 2 needs a per-lane find and a fourth rename stage (+1.7% mean, +9.2% worst on the OI-34 sweep). Home-only (8 candidates, not 24) costs nothing on the sweep. Idle enables none. Floors 2 under the measure.

MIU's kept lead, each slot's m_hi_cr02h, m_lo_cr02h and m_am_cr02h (46 flops, one gate a slot). Its predicate-write lead (phys_pred, active_mask) is on ccv_miu_rcu_data only in T-1 (RA-40: the payload's own fields, leading, not copies), and the write and the guard forward need it in T, so this module keeps it a cycle. Nothing earlier names the write, so the only enable is the lead's own valid & pred_we, straight from RCU's interface flop on the channel (DA's ruling on RI-11: a flop at every block boundary; rcu_pred.ngd.json, arrival 0): the enable starts at a flop and its cone is one AND, within CG-2's 8. Loaded every cycle instead, the 4 x 46 flops would be 184 ungated flops against this module's 2% (57). Allowed by Daniel's ruling on RI-15 (RA rev 87, DA rev 109, 2026-11-06): module-level CG waivers for interface lead signals, each lead flop charged to the RCU block's per-instance 2%, to fit at final construction. The enable's arrival rose to the fanout term (mwe_cr01h 1.4; AR 326, RA rev 106), so it reads 3.1: cone 1.7 plus 1.4, still within CG-2's 8.

Each slot's guard lead kept for A, g_gl's rg_hi_cr02h and rg_lo_cr02h (14 flops a slot; check-only rgu_cr02h and rgz_cr02h beside them), named in the netlist by the read wires g_guard[s].hi_cr02h and lo_cr02h; on R, its predicate sources rimm_cr02h (14 flops, lead_rpsrc[13:0]) share the gate. RA-43 took phys_pred_guard out of the payload, and R's imm out of R's: lead_guard_pred and lead_rpsrc are on ccv_ooe_rcu_issue only in A-1, beside the slot's valid, and are kept for A here (RA-31, RA-32, the split guard read, now on every slot). Nothing earlier names the issue, so the only enable is that valid, a wire from the zero-cycle end (rcu_pred.ngd.json, iv_cr01h 2.1). One gate a slot, nine gates, 140 flops: loaded every cycle instead they would be far past this module's 2%. Allowed by Daniel's ruling on RI-15 (RA rev 87, DA rev 109, 2026-11-06): module-level CG waivers for interface lead signals, each lead flop charged to the RCU block's per-instance 2%, to fit at final construction. The enable's arrival is the fanout term (iv_cr01h 2.1, slot 8's valid at 68 loads; AR 326, RA rev 106), within CG-2's 8.

R's moved leads kept for A, imm_cr02h (32 flops) and rrow_cr02h (16 flops), one gate: RA-43 took R's imm and source rows out of its payload, and lead_rpsrc (movi's literal, call's link, the shuffles' lane and the predicate sources) and lead_phys_src are on ccv_ooe_rcu_issue only in A-1, beside R's valid; this capture holds them in A as the payload would (the schema's lead_why). rrow_cr02h is a copy of its own ((* keep *)), since it drives an output, the slices' R reads in A (rr_row_cr02h). The only enable is that valid, a wire from the zero-cycle end (rcu_r.ngd.json, iv_cr01h 2.1), within CG-2's 8. Loaded every cycle instead, the 48 flops would put the module past its 2%. Allowed by Daniel's ruling on RI-15 (RA rev 87, DA rev 109, 2026-11-06): module-level CG waivers for interface lead signals, each lead flop charged to the RCU block's per-instance 2%, to fit at final construction.

PC's merge mask (~active of S slot k's predicate-only copy, P7, 4 x 32 flops), one gate a slot, loaded under the PC's own valid (pcq, a flop). A mask changes on about 1 - 0.5^2 = 75% of its loads under the bench's active draw (all ones half the time, test/rcu/lanes_tb.cpp), so each gate sits at CG-3's 75% by chance: measured 61-74% in medium (slot 2 at 61% over 41 loads), 73-74% in high, the others at 75% or over (check-cg --unit rcu_lanes at c8dbab0; real traffic's all-ones runs would read lower still). Sharing lact's stage-2 gate (the same data a cycle on) took lact's own 64 flops a slot under 75% with it, and an enable on the mask's change would read an input (CG-5). Floors 2 points under the lowest gate in each scenario; idle never loads. TI re-measured on the merged tree with RA-43 (full gate on 7ee18501, 2026-11-09): slot 1 at 51% over 51 loads in medium, slot 0 at 67% over 215 in high, the same draw by chance; floors re-set 2 under (OI-18: RI to confirm).

The slot's class word, cls_cr02h (26 flops after synthesis: class bits 25 and 26 are equal and merge), and its lead copies x_cr02h (RA 131 (1): lead_cont and lead_pred_neg on every slot, and on S0-S3 lead_phys_src, lead_phys_old_dst, lead_old_dst_pos and lead_src_pos; 2 flops, or 34 on S0-S3), one gate: RA-43 decodes the op class into flops at A-1 from the slot's lead fields (lead_opcode, lead_done_row, lead_pred_we, lead_phys_dst), and the copies of the payload fields whose in-path from the zero-cycle end was over 12 ride the same capture, so their readers (rcu_pred, rcu_lanes) take them from flops in A. The leads are on ccv_ooe_rcu_issue only in A-1, beside the slot's valid (RA rev 117; one shared capture for the block, RI-25). Nothing earlier names the issue, so the only enable is that valid, a wire from the zero-cycle end (rcu_isd.ngd.json, iv_cr01h 2.1, the fanout term of slot 8's valid at 68 loads; AR 326, RA rev 106), within CG-2's 8. Loaded every cycle instead, 9 x 26 + 146 flops would be ungated against the block's 2%. Allowed by Daniel's ruling on RI-15 (RA rev 87, DA rev 109, 2026-11-06): module-level CG waivers for interface lead signals, each lead flop charged to the RCU block's per-instance 2% (9 x 26 + 4 x 34 + 5 x 2 = 380), to fit at final construction.
